static_traits.name: Li Qian
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with daughters somewhat strained by self-blame; having a supportive spouse, but finding it difficult to discuss these feelings with family
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problem history in the past; never received psychotherapy before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, well organized, able to self-reflect and cooperate; slightly tense emotionally but highly cooperative

basic_info.main_problem: Because the daughters did not catch any fish while fishing with me, I feel I am a terrible fishing teacher.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of inadequacy and self-blame have affected my relationship with the daughters and my enjoyment of fishing, prompting me to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I am a terrible / incompetent teacher (parent)
Whether the student (daughter) succeeds depends entirely on me

special_situations.event: Repeated experiences of going fishing with the daughters where no one caught anything
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I were a good teacher, they should be able to catch fish; otherwise it is my failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly intensifying teaching and skill training, taking all responsibility on myself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They did not catch fish; it is all my fault, I am a terrible teacher

special_situations.event: During fishing the daughters showed enjoyment and excitement, but still did not catch any fish
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only the result of catching fish counts as success; the joy in the process does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores positive experiences, focuses excessively on the single result of 'whether a fish was caught'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They did not catch fish; this time counts as a failure

special_situations.event: Still no successful catch after multiple fishing trips; pressure intensifying
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A good teacher should ensure students reach their goals; if they have not, the teacher is unqualified
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets rigid high standards and harsh demands for himself, driving improvement through self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As long as they have not caught anything, I am just a failure

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a good mother / good teacher who brings success and happiness, recognized and needed by the daughters
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointing the daughters and being seen as incompetent, thereby damaging the emotional bond with the daughters
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control over outcomes by attributing all responsibility to oneself
Harshly blaming myself with high standards to avoid facing uncontrollable factors (luck, interest, learning stage)

object_relations.self_representation: Incompetent, a teacher / mother who needs to constantly make up for failure
object_relations.object_representation: Daughters who need me to guarantee results and may be disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes the positive side of parent-child interaction (e.g. the daughters enjoying the process, bonding, and memories)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating attention to the positive side with ignoring the 'failure' of not catching fish, worrying this means admitting incompetence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly saying 'It is all my problem / I did not teach well' in a gentle but self-blaming tone, downplaying external factors; judging myself by abstract standards, avoiding present emotional experience.

manifestations: Reduces the meaning of fishing to 'whether a fish is caught', ignoring the value of parent-child companionship and connection
Tying self-worth to results; dismissing myself whenever no fish is caught yet
outcomes: Reduced interest and pleasure in fishing as a hobby

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly judging myself by the rigid standard of 'a good teacher should ensure student success'
Internalizes 'whether a fish bites' as the only standard of success

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: When talking about positive experiences, quickly returns to one's own faults and responsibility attribution
Maintains a sense of control over outcomes through self-blame, limiting engagement with present enjoyment

positive_force: Spouse is supportive and willing to listen
The daughters enjoy the time and companionship during fishing; there is a basis for positive parent-child interaction
The client has a positive attitude and is willing to do cognitive restructuring and reality testing
Occupational functioning not yet affected, with some psychological resilience
negative_force: An attribution style that fully personalizes outcomes (self-blame)
Rigid 'should' standards and high expectations (performance-oriented self-worth)
Dismissing positive experiences, over-focusing on failure evidence
Difficulty communicating emotions with family leads to limited use of support

target_behavior.behavior: Recurring self-blame and negative automatic thoughts in situations related to fishing with the daughters
antecedent: The daughters not yet able to catch fish when going fishing
Recalling past experiences of no catch or planning the next fishing trip
target_behavior.core_reason: Having internalized the rule 'a good teacher must ensure student success', adopting personalized attribution, treating uncontrollable factors (luck, learning stage, interest differences) as personal failure
target_behavior.function: Gaining a subjective sense of control over the situation and trying to drive improvement through self-blame, while avoiding acknowledging the helplessness brought by external uncontrollability
target_behavior.consequence: Parent-child relationship tension, increased pressure and sense of loss, decreased interest and pleasure in fishing
